short.title: Psachna Tomb: 3200-Year-Old Mycenaean Giant Found #Shorts
short.hook: Greek road workers unearthed a massive 3,200-year-old Mycenaean tomb near Psachna.
script: Greek road workers unearthed a massive 3,200-year-old Mycenaean tomb near Psachna.
It ranks among the 20 largest known tholos tombs in Greece.
Built with corbelling, it shows advanced stone engineering without true arches.
Its size suggests elite status, but no royal or dynasty link has been confirmed.
Could it have held a single ruler or a family of heirs?
The tomb reveals Euboea’s independent elite power in the Late Bronze Age.
Did local elites mirror mainland Mycenaean power structures?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A massive 3,200-year-old Mycenaean tholos tomb was uncovered near Psachna on Euboea. It ranks among the 20 largest known such tombs in Greece, suggesting it was built for a wealthy elite. Early reports called it a royal tomb, but archaeologists have not confirmed any royal or dynastic link. The tomb’s corbelling construction shows sophisticated stone engineering. Its discovery raises questions about social hierarchy and political organization in Late Bronze Age Euboea. Source: newsfire.gr, https://newsfire.gr/en/greek-road-workers-unearth-massive-3200-year-old-mycenaean-tomb/
